claim: Candida albicans is both a member of the healthy human microbiome and a major pathogen in immunocompromised individuals.
source_text: Candida albicans is both a member of the healthy human microbiome and a major pathogen in immunocompromised individuals.
evidence_reasoning: This is established scientific knowledge about C. albicans' dual role as commensal and pathogen.

claim: C. albicans infections are typically treated with azole inhibitors of ergosterol biosynthesis.
source_text: Infections are typically treated with azole inhibitors of ergosterol biosynthesis often leading to drug resistance.
evidence_reasoning: This reflects standard clinical practice and established treatment protocols.

claim: Azole treatment of C. albicans infections often leads to drug resistance.
source_text: Infections are typically treated with azole inhibitors of ergosterol biosynthesis often leading to drug resistance.
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by clinical observations and referenced literature on drug resistance emergence.

claim: The study analyzed 43 isolates from 11 oral candidiasis patients using next-generation sequencing.
source_text: Here, we leveraged next-generation sequencing to analyze 43 isolates from 11 oral candidiasis patients.
evidence_reasoning: This describes the experimental design and sample size of the study.

claim: LOH events were commonly associated with acquired resistance in the studied isolates.
source_text: LOH events were commonly associated with acquired resistance
evidence_reasoning: This is a primary finding from the genomic analysis of the clinical isolates.

claim: SNPs in 240 genes may be related to host adaptation.
source_text: SNPs in 240 genes may be related to host adaptation.
evidence_reasoning: This is derived from computational analysis of recurrent persistent SNPs across patient series.

claim: Most aneuploidies were transient and did not correlate with drug resistance.
source_text: Conversely, most aneuploidies were transient and did not correlate with drug resistance.
evidence_reasoning: This finding is based on analysis of chromosomal copy number variations across isolates.

claim: Isolates varied in adherence, filamentation, and virulence phenotypes.
source_text: Our analysis also shows that isolates also varied in adherence, filamentation, and virulence.
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by experimental measurements of these phenotypes.

claim: Virtually all humans are colonized with Candida albicans.
source_text: Virtually all humans are colonized with Candida albicans
evidence_reasoning: This is established epidemiological knowledge about C. albicans colonization.

claim: C. albicans possesses phenotypic switching as a trait that promotes pathogenicity.
source_text: C. albicans possesses an arsenal of traits that promote its pathogenicity, including phenotypic switching
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by citation to Alby and Bennett, 2009.

claim: C. albicans possesses yeast-hyphae transition as a trait that promotes pathogenicity.
source_text: C. albicans possesses an arsenal of traits that promote its pathogenicity, including...yeast–hyphae transition
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by citation to Kumamoto and Vinces, 2005.

claim: C. albicans secretes molecules that promote adhesion to abiotic surfaces.
source_text: C. albicans possesses an arsenal of traits that promote its pathogenicity, including...the secretion of molecules that promote adhesion to abiotic surfaces
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by citation to Chandra et al., 2001.

claim: Systemic C. albicans infections are fatal in 42% of cases despite antifungal therapies.
source_text: systemic C. albicans infections are fatal in 42% of cases (Wisplinghoff et al., 2003), despite the use of antifungal therapies
evidence_reasoning: This mortality statistic is cited from Wisplinghoff et al., 2003.

claim: C. albicans is the fourth most common infection in hospitals.
source_text: C. albicans is the fourth most common infection in hospitals
evidence_reasoning: This epidemiological fact is cited from Gudlaugsson et al., 2003 and Pappas et al., 2003.

claim: Two classes of antifungals in clinical use target ergosterol: polyenes and azoles.
source_text: Two classes of antifungals in clinical use target ergosterol, a major component of the fungal cell membrane: polyenes and azoles.
evidence_reasoning: This describes established antifungal drug classes and their mechanism.

claim: Polyenes (e.g., Amphotericin B) are used sparingly due to toxicity.
source_text: Polyenes (e.g., Amphotericin B) are used sparingly due to toxicity
evidence_reasoning: This clinical practice is supported by citation to Rex et al., 1994.

claim: Azoles (e.g., fluconazole) are used widely because they can be administered orally and have few side effects.
source_text: azoles (e.g., fluconazole) are used widely because they can be administered orally and have few side effects
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by citation to Rex et al., 2003.

claim: Resistance to azoles arises within the commensal population of the treated individual primarily because azoles are fungistatic.
source_text: resistance to the azoles arises within the commensal population of the treated individual, primarily because azoles are fungistatic (inhibit growth but do not kill)
evidence_reasoning: This mechanism is supported by citation to Cowen et al., 2002.

claim: The intensity of fluconazole use is driving the appearance of resistant isolates.
source_text: Epidemiological data suggest that the intensity of fluconazole use is driving the appearance of resistant isolates
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by epidemiological data cited from Pfaller et al., 1998.

claim: Drug resistance can increase during infection through the acquisition of aneuploidies due to genomic plasticity.
source_text: Studies of clinical isolates of C. albicans suggest that drug resistance can increase during an infection through the acquisition of aneuploidies (Selmecki et al., 2009) due to genomic plasticity
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by citation to Selmecki et al., 2009.

claim: Increased activity or level of ergosterol pathway enzymes (e.g., ERG11) reduces direct impact of the drug on its target.
source_text: First, increased activity or level of the enzymes of the ergosterol pathway (e.g., ERG11) reduces direct impact of the drug on its target
evidence_reasoning: This mechanism is supported by citations to Asai et al., 1999 and Oliver et al., 2007.

claim: Increased efflux of the drug by ABC transporters (CDR1 and CDR2) reduces the effective intracellular drug concentration.
source_text: Second, increased efflux of the drug from cells by ABC transporters (encoded by CDR1 and CDR2) (Coste et al., 2006)...reduces the effective intracellular drug concentration.
evidence_reasoning: This mechanism is supported by citation to Coste et al., 2006.

claim: Increased efflux by the major facilitator superfamily efflux pump (MDR1) reduces the effective intracellular drug concentration.
source_text: increased efflux of the drug from cells by...the major facilitator superfamily efflux pump (encoded by MDR1) (Dunkel et al., 2008) reduces the effective intracellular drug concentration.
evidence_reasoning: This mechanism is supported by citation to Dunkel et al., 2008.

claim: Point mutations in genes encoding resistance proteins can result in azole resistance.
source_text: such alterations can result from point mutations in genes encoding these proteins
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by citation to Marichal et al., 1999.

claim: Point mutations in transcription factors that regulate mRNA expression levels can result in azole resistance.
source_text: such alterations can result from...point mutations in...transcription factors that regulate mRNA expression levels
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by citations to MacPherson et al., 2005, Coste et al., 2006, and Dunkel et al., 2008.

claim: Increased copy number of relevant genes via genome rearrangements can result in azole resistance.
source_text: such alterations can result from...increased copy number of the relevant genes, via genome rearrangements such as whole chromosome and segmental aneuploidies
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by citations to Selmecki et al., 2006, 2008, 2009.

claim: Drug-resistant strains isolated following clinical treatment often exhibit loss of heterozygosity (LOH).
source_text: the genomes of drug-resistant strains isolated following clinical treatment often exhibit large-scale changes, such as loss of heterozygosity (LOH)
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by citations to Coste et al., 2006 and Dunkel and Morschhauser, 2011.

claim: Drug-resistant strains often exhibit copy-number variation (CNV), including short segmental CNV.
source_text: the genomes of drug-resistant strains isolated following clinical treatment often exhibit large-scale changes, such as...copy-number variation (CNV), including short segmental CNV
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by citation to Selmecki et al., 2010.

claim: Drug-resistant strains often exhibit whole chromosome aneuploidy accompanied by point mutations.
source_text: the genomes of drug-resistant strains isolated following clinical treatment often exhibit large-scale changes, such as...whole chromosome aneuploidy (Selmecki et al., 2010) accompanied by point mutations.
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by citation to Selmecki et al., 2010.

claim: It is challenging to use forward genetic approaches in C. albicans due to its diploid genome and lack of a complete sexual cycle.
source_text: It is challenging to use forward genetic approaches in C. albicans due to its diploid genome and lack of a complete sexual cycle.
evidence_reasoning: This reflects established limitations in C. albicans genetics.

claim: C. albicans has conserved the genomic elements needed for mating.
source_text: Although C. albicans has conserved the genomic elements needed for mating
evidence_reasoning: This is established knowledge about C. albicans genomic content.

claim: C. albicans mating occurs through rare mating-competent haploids.
source_text: mating occurs instead through rare mating-competent haploids
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by citation to Hickman et al., 2013.

claim: C. albicans mating occurs via a parasexual cycle consisting of mating of diploid strains to form tetraploids followed by chromosome loss to regenerate diploids.
source_text: mating occurs...via a parasexual cycle consisting of mating of diploid strains to form tetraploids followed by chromosome loss to regenerate diploids
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by citation to Bennett and Johnson, 2005.

claim: Previous studies in evolved isolates have focused on large-scale aberrations such as aneuploidies and LOH.
source_text: Studies in evolved isolates have implicated multiple mechanisms in drug resistance, but have focused on large-scale aberrations such as aneuploidies and LOH
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by citations to Selmecki et al., 2008, 2009.

claim: Previous studies in evolved isolates have focused on candidate genes but do not comprehensively chart the genetic basis of adaptation.
source_text: Studies in evolved isolates have implicated multiple mechanisms in drug resistance, but have focused on...candidate genes (Perea et al., 2001; White et al., 2002), and do not comprehensively chart the genetic basis of adaptation.
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by citations to Perea et al., 2001 and White et al., 2002.

claim: The study used genome sequencing of isolates sampled consecutively from patients clinically treated with fluconazole.
source_text: we used genome sequencing of isolates sampled consecutively from patients that were clinically treated with fluconazole
evidence_reasoning: This describes the study design and methodology.

claim: Most isolates from each individual patient were highly related, suggesting a clonal population structure.
source_text: Most isolates from each individual patient were highly related, suggesting a clonal population structure
evidence_reasoning: This is a finding from phylogenetic analysis of the sequencing data.

claim: Each clinical sample was purified from a single colony.
source_text: Because each clinical sample was purified from a single colony, we cannot assess the population structure at any single time point.
evidence_reasoning: This describes the sampling methodology.

claim: The study cannot assess the population structure at any single time point due to single colony sampling.
source_text: Because each clinical sample was purified from a single colony, we cannot assess the population structure at any single time point.
evidence_reasoning: This is a logical limitation inferred from the sampling method.

claim: LOH events were recurrent across patients' series and were associated with increased drug resistance.
source_text: Consistent with previous studies, we found that LOH events were recurrent across patients' series and were associated with increased drug resistance.
evidence_reasoning: This is a primary finding from the genomic analysis.

claim: The study identified 240 genes that recurrently contain persistent SNPs.
source_text: We found 240 genes that recurrently contain persistent SNPs
evidence_reasoning: This is a quantitative result from the computational analysis.

claim: Many of the 240 recurrently mutated genes may be related to antifungal exposure and adaptation to the host.
source_text: We found 240 genes that recurrently contain persistent SNPs, many of which may be related not only to antifungal exposure but also to the complex process of adaptation to the host and antifungal exposure.
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from the recurrence patterns and functional annotations of the genes.

claim: Aneuploidies were prevalent in the isolates.
source_text: In contrast, aneuploidies were prevalent in the isolates
evidence_reasoning: This is a finding from copy number analysis.

claim: Aneuploidies were more likely to be transient.
source_text: aneuploidies were prevalent in the isolates, yet they were more likely to be transient
evidence_reasoning: This is observed from temporal analysis of aneuploidy patterns.

claim: Aneuploidy per se did not correlate with changes in drug resistance.
source_text: aneuploidy, per se, did not correlate with changes in drug resistance
evidence_reasoning: This is a finding from correlation analysis between aneuploidy and MIC.

claim: The isolates were obtained from HIV-infected patients with oropharyngeal candidiasis.
source_text: Isolates were obtained from HIV-infected patients with oropharyngeal candidiasis
evidence_reasoning: This describes the patient population and sample source.

claim: The patients were not on azole antifungal treatment at time of enrollment.
source_text: The patients were not on azole antifungal treatment at time of enrollment
evidence_reasoning: This describes the initial treatment status of the patients.

claim: Subsequent samples were collected during recurrence of infection.
source_text: subsequent samples were collected during recurrence of infection
evidence_reasoning: This describes the sampling timeline.

claim: Isolates were colony purified at collection and represent a single clone.
source_text: Isolates were colony purified at collection and represent a single clone.

claim: Genomic DNA was sequenced using Illumina sequencing with 53-283X coverage, 103X on average.
source_text: We sequenced the genomic DNA of the isolates as well as the C. albicans lab strain, SC5314, using Illumina sequencing (53-283X coverage, 103X on average
evidence_reasoning: This describes the sequencing methodology and coverage.

claim: The study validated the SNP detection pipeline using Sequenom iPlex genotyping.
source_text: We validated our pipeline for detection of point mutations using Sequenom iPlex genotyping
evidence_reasoning: This describes the validation methodology.

claim: The iPlex base calls matched 1853 (93.9%) of the calls from computational analysis of the sequencing data.
source_text: We interrogated 1973 SNPs in 27 isolates from nine clinical series and found that the iPlex base calls matched 1853 (93.9%, Figure 1—figure supplement 1A, Table 2) of the calls from our computational analysis of the sequencing data.
evidence_reasoning: This is a quantitative validation result.

claim: At least one non-clonal C. albicans isolate was detected in three of the ten patient series (PT 9, 16, 42).
source_text: we detected at least one non-clonal C. albicans isolate in three of the remaining ten patient series (PT 9,16, 42; Figure 2B, red)
evidence_reasoning: This is a finding from phylogenetic analysis.

claim: At least ~36% of the 11 patients sampled carried more than one unrelated Candida strain.
source_text: indicating that at least ∼36% of the 11 patients sampled carried more than one unrelated Candida strain
evidence_reasoning: This is calculated from the number of patients with non-clonal isolates.

claim: Patient 64 contained one C. albicans isolate (4018) and one C. dubliniensis isolate (4380).
source_text: Patient 64 contained one C. albicans isolate (4018) and one C. dubliniensis isolate (4380)
evidence_reasoning: This is a finding from sequence alignment analysis.

claim: Each isolate typically differed by several thousand SNPs from its progenitor isolate.
source_text: the distance between isolates indicated significant genetic diversity within each patient series (Figure 2B), typically with each isolate differing by several thousand SNPs from its 'progenitor' isolate
evidence_reasoning: This is a quantitative finding from SNP analysis.

claim: Different isolates collected on the same day from the same patient (patient 14 [2440 and 2501]) differed by 9668 SNPs.
source_text: different isolates collected on the same day from the same patient (patient 14 [2440 and 2501] and patient 16 [3107 and 3119]) differed by 9668 and 18,291 SNPs, respectively
evidence_reasoning: This is a specific quantitative finding demonstrating within-patient diversity.

claim: Different isolates collected on the same day from patient 16 (3107 and 3119) differed by 18,291 SNPs.
source_text: different isolates collected on the same day from the same patient (patient 14 [2440 and 2501] and patient 16 [3107 and 3119]) differed by 9668 and 18,291 SNPs, respectively

claim: Same-day isolates from the same patient had very different fluconazole MIC levels.
source_text: different isolates collected on the same day from the same patient...had very different fluconazole MIC levels
evidence_reasoning: This is from MIC measurements of same-day isolates.

claim: A population of related but divergent genotypes of the same lineage exists within a given patient.
source_text: Thus, we conclude that a population of related but divergent genotypes of the same lineage exists within a given patient.
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from the genetic diversity observed within clonal patient series.

claim: Persistent changes include variants that were driven to sufficiently high frequency by selection to ensure repeated sampling.
source_text: We reasoned that such persistent changes will include those variants that were driven to sufficiently high frequency by selection to ensure repeated sampling
evidence_reasoning: This is a logical inference about the meaning of persistence in the context of sampling.

claim: LOH events were detected in all of the series.
source_text: LOH events were detected in all of the series
evidence_reasoning: This is a finding from LOH analysis across all patient series.

claim: LOH events were often persistent.
source_text: LOH events were detected in all of the series and were often persistent

claim: LOH events were recurrent across patient series.
source_text: LOH events were detected in all of the series and were often persistent, recurrent

claim: LOH events were associated with increased drug resistance.
source_text: LOH events were detected in all of the series and were often persistent, recurrent, and associated with increased drug resistance

claim: Putative driver mutations were identified in 17 genes.
source_text: Putative driver mutations...were identified in 17 genes

claim: ERG11 was affected in 70% (7/10) of the patient series.
source_text: ERG11, which encodes the drug target of fluconazole, was affected in 70% (7/10) of the patient series

claim: Aneuploidies were evident in at least one isolate from 80% (8/10) of the clonal patient series.
source_text: Aneuploidies, either whole chromosomal or segmental, were evident in at least one isolate from 80% (8/10) of the clonal patient series

claim: The most prevalent aneuploidies involved Chromosome 5 (6 of 8 patients with at least one aneuploid isolate).
source_text: the most prevalent aneuploidies involving Chromosome 5 (6 of 8 patients with at least one aneuploid isolate

claim: Persistent aneuploidies were rarer than persistent LOH events.
source_text: In contrast to the persistence of most LOH events, persistent aneuploidies were rarer
evidence_reasoning: This is a comparative finding from temporal analysis.

claim: Persistent aneuploidies were not consistently associated with adaptive increases in MIC levels.
source_text: persistent aneuploidies were rarer and were not consistently associated with adaptive increases in MIC levels
evidence_reasoning: This is from correlation analysis between persistent aneuploidy and MIC.

claim: Aneuploidy could contribute to the evolution of LOH by increasing the likelihood of its occurrence.
source_text: we hypothesize that aneuploidy could contribute to the evolution of LOH by increasing the likelihood of its occurrence
evidence_reasoning: This is a hypothesis based on observed patterns but not directly tested.

claim: In 4 of the 6 patients with a Chromosome 5 LOH, the isolate with an LOH event also harbors a Chromosome 5 trisomy or is preceded by an isolate with a Chromosome 5 trisomy.
source_text: For example, in 4 of the 6 patients with a Chromosome 5 LOH, the isolate with an LOH event also harbors a Chromosome 5 trisomy or is preceded by an isolate with a Chromosome 5 trisomy.

claim: The study identified persistent nonsynonymous coding SNPs within 1470 genes outside LOH tracts.
source_text: We identified persistent nonsynonymous coding SNPs within 1470 genes outside LOH tracts
evidence_reasoning: This is a quantitative result from SNP analysis.

claim: 167 genes harbored 336 driver-like polymorphisms.
source_text: 167 of them harboring 336 driver-like polymorphisms
evidence_reasoning: This is a quantitative result from driver mutation analysis.

claim: The number of 240 recurrently mutated genes is higher than expected by chance (empirical p < 10−4).
source_text: This number of genes is higher than expected by chance (empirical p < 10−4 based on a Poisson model of background mutation
evidence_reasoning: This is from statistical modeling comparing observed to expected recurrence.

claim: The coding sequence for the 240 recurrent genes is longer than average (2.21 ± 1.53 kb vs 1.83 ± 1.29 kb for non-recurrent persistent genes, p < 3.68 × 10−5).
source_text: the coding sequence for these 240 recurrent genes is longer than average (2.21 ± 1.53 kb vs 1.83 ± 1.29 kb for non-recurrent persistent genes, p < 3.68 × 10−5, t-test)
evidence_reasoning: This is a quantitative finding from gene length analysis.

claim: 17 persistent recurrently polymorphic genes also had driver-like polymorphisms.
source_text: Notably, 17 persistent recurrently polymorphic genes also had driver-like polymorphisms
evidence_reasoning: This is from overlap analysis of recurrent and driver mutations.

claim: Eight of the 17 genes with driver-like polymorphisms were also homozygosed in an LOH tract in at least one patient series.
source_text: 17 persistent recurrently polymorphic genes also had driver-like polymorphisms, eight of which were also homozygosed in an LOH tract in at least one patient series
evidence_reasoning: This is from overlap analysis of driver mutations and LOH regions.

claim: Polymorphisms in 166 of the 240 genes appeared together with an increase in MIC.
source_text: polymorphisms in 166 of the 240 genes appeared together with an increase in MIC
evidence_reasoning: This is from correlation analysis between mutations and MIC changes.

claim: The set of 240 recurrently mutated genes was enriched for fungal-type cell wall genes (18 genes, p < 0.0012).
source_text: The set of 240 recurrently mutated genes was enriched for fungal-type cell wall (18 genes, p < 0.0012)
evidence_reasoning: This is from gene ontology enrichment analysis.

claim: The set of 240 recurrently mutated genes was enriched for cell surface genes (24 genes, p < 0.00012).
source_text: The set of 240 recurrently mutated genes was enriched for...cell surface genes (24 genes, p < 0.00012)
evidence_reasoning: This is from gene ontology enrichment analysis.

claim: The recurrently mutated genes include several members of three cell wall gene families important for biofilm formation and virulence: the Hyr/Iff proteins, the ALS adhesins, and the PGA-30-like proteins.
source_text: including several members in each of three cell wall gene families important for biofilm formation and virulence (Hoyer et al., 2008): the Hyr/Iff proteins (HYR1 and 3, IFF8 and 6), the ALS adhesins (ALS1-4,7,9), and the PGA-30-like proteins (seven genes)
evidence_reasoning: This is from functional annotation of recurrent genes with citation to their known roles.

claim: All three cell wall gene families are specifically expanded in the genomes of pathogenic Candida species.
source_text: All three families are specifically expanded in the genomes of pathogenic Candida species
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by citation to Butler et al., 2009.

claim: Seven members of the FGR genes, involved in filamentous growth and specifically expanded in C. albicans, are among the 240 genes.
source_text: seven members of the FGR genes (Uhl et al., 2003), involved in filamentous growth and specifically expanded in C. albicans (Butler et al., 2009), are also among the 240 genes
evidence_reasoning: This is from functional annotation with citations to known gene functions.

claim: The most recurrently mutated gene outside of an LOH region was AXL1.
source_text: The most recurrently mutated gene outside of an LOH region was AXL1
evidence_reasoning: This is from ranking genes by recurrence frequency.

claim: AXL1 encodes a putative endoprotease whose transcript is upregulated in an RHE model of oral candidiasis and in clinical isolates from HIV+ patients with oral candidiasis.
source_text: AXL1 that encodes a putative endoprotease, whose transcript is upregulated in an RHE model of oral candidiasis and in clinical isolates from HIV+ patients with oral candidiasis
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by citation to Zakikhany et al., 2007.

claim: AXL1 is persistently mutated in eight series, three of which were driver mutations.
source_text: The gene is persistently mutated in eight series, (three of which were driver mutations)
evidence_reasoning: This is a quantitative finding from mutation analysis.

claim: ERG11 was affected with persistent SNPs in four series (Patients 9, 14, 30, and 59).
source_text: ERG11, which encodes the drug target of fluconazole, was affected in 70% (7/10) of the patient series with persistent SNPs in four series (Patients 9, 14, 30, and 59)
evidence_reasoning: This is a specific finding from mutation analysis.

claim: ERG11 had mutations in LOH events in three series (Patients 1, 15, and 43).
source_text: ERG11...was affected in 70% (7/10) of the patient series with persistent SNPs in four series (Patients 9, 14, 30, and 59) and mutations in the LOH events in three series (Patients 1, 15, and 43)
evidence_reasoning: This is a specific finding from LOH and mutation analysis.

claim: HYR3, a known virulence gene, was persistently mutated in nine of the patients.
source_text: Likewise HYR3, a known virulence gene, was persistently mutated in nine of the patients
evidence_reasoning: This is a quantitative finding from mutation analysis.

claim: The 240 recurrently mutated genes were partitioned into 5 co-occurrence clusters based on correlation in their mutation occurrence patterns.
source_text: we partitioned the 240 recurrently mutated genes into 5 'co-occurrence clusters' based on the correlation in their mutation occurrence patterns
evidence_reasoning: This is from clustering analysis of mutation patterns.

claim: The correlations in co-occurrence clusters are significantly higher than expected in a null model (p < 5.2 × 10−182).
source_text: These correlations are significantly higher than expected in a null model (p < 5.2 × 10−182, permutation test
evidence_reasoning: This is from statistical testing against a permutation-based null model.

claim: Cluster 1 is enriched for cell wall and cell surface genes.
source_text: Cluster 1 is enriched for cell wall and cell surface genes
evidence_reasoning: This is from gene ontology enrichment analysis of the cluster.

claim: Cluster 2 is enriched for cell cycle and stress genes.
source_text: Cluster 2 for cell cycle and stress genes
evidence_reasoning: This is from gene ontology enrichment analysis of the cluster.

claim: Cluster 3 is enriched for genes involved in drug response.
source_text: Cluster 3 for genes involved in drug response
evidence_reasoning: This is from gene ontology enrichment analysis of the cluster.

claim: Cluster 5 is enriched for carbohydrate binding genes.
source_text: Cluster 5 for carbohydrate binding
evidence_reasoning: This is from gene ontology enrichment analysis of the cluster.

claim: Adhesion, filamentation, and virulence in a C. elegans model of infection varied substantially between isolates in the same series.
source_text: We found substantial variation in many of these phenotypes between isolates in the same series
evidence_reasoning: This is from experimental measurements of these phenotypes.

claim: Increased fitness in vitro (in the absence of drug) generally correlated with an increase in traits associated with virulence.
source_text: In general, increased fitness in vitro (in the absence of drug) correlated with an increase in traits associated with virulence (adhesion, filamentation, and virulence in nematode).
evidence_reasoning: This is from correlation analysis of fitness and virulence measurements.

claim: The later isolates in the series from patients 30 and 43 had increased fitness and higher virulence by all three measures.
source_text: For example, the later isolates in the series from patients 30 and 43 had increased fitness and higher virulence by all three measures
evidence_reasoning: This is from experimental measurements of fitness and virulence phenotypes.

claim: A decrease in fitness in isolate 13 of patient 1 was accompanied by a decrease in virulence.
source_text: whereas, a decrease in fitness in isolate 13 of patient 1 was accompanied by a decrease in virulence
evidence_reasoning: This is from experimental measurements of fitness and virulence phenotypes.

claim: In patient 59, fitness in vitro decreased while virulence phenotypes increased in a later isolate.
source_text: A notable exception was patient 59, where fitness in vitro decreased while virulence phenotypes increased in a later isolate
evidence_reasoning: This is from experimental measurements showing an exception to the general trend.

claim: In vitro fitness is not always a reflection of virulence.
source_text: This is consistent with the observations of Noble and co-workers that in vitro fitness is not always a reflection of virulence
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by citation to Noble et al., 2010 and the data from patient 59.

claim: Initially in a series, drug resistance (MIC) and in vitro fitness (in the absence of drug) were inversely related.
source_text: Initially in a series, drug resistance (MIC) and in vitro fitness (in the absence of drug) were inversely related
evidence_reasoning: This is from correlation analysis of MIC and fitness measurements.

claim: When MIC increases first appeared, they were usually accompanied by a decrease in fitness in the absence of drug.
source_text: When MIC increases first appeared, they were usually accompanied by a decrease in fitness in the absence of drug (Patient 1, isolates 2, 13, and 16, Patients 9, 14, 15 16, and 59
evidence_reasoning: This is from temporal analysis of MIC and fitness measurements.

claim: Isolates with elevated MIC exhibited increased relative fitness in the presence of the drug.
source_text: Consistent with the elevated MIC, these isolates exhibited increased relative fitness in the presence of the drug
evidence_reasoning: This is from fitness measurements in the presence of fluconazole.

claim: Resistance conferred by gain-of-function mutations in transcription factors Mrr1, Tac1, and Upc2 is associated with reduced fitness under non-selective conditions in vitro and in vivo.
source_text: This is also consistent with a recent study (Sasse et al., 2012) showing that resistance conferred in C. albicans by gain-of-function mutations in the transcription factors Mrr1, Tac1, and Upc2 is associated with reduced fitness under non-selective conditions in vitro as well as in vivo during colonization of a mammalian host.
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by citation to Sasse et al., 2012.

claim: Isolates from later time points were often more fit than those from earlier time points without further changes in MIC.
source_text: Consistent with subsequent selection of strains with compensatory variations, isolates from later time points were often more fit than those from earlier time points (measured in vitro, in the absence of drug) without further changes in MIC
evidence_reasoning: This is from temporal analysis of fitness and MIC measurements.

claim: Compensatory mutations may arise to offset the major fitness cost of mutations conferring drug resistance.
source_text: This general trend is consistent with previous studies in bacteria (Bjorkman and Andersson, 2000); (Gagneux et al., 2006) and in a single documented case in C. glabrata (Singh-Babak et al., 2012), suggesting that compensatory mutations may subsequently arise to offset the major fitness cost of mutations conferring drug resistance.
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from the data and supported by citations to similar findings in other organisms.

claim: Aneuploidies may be an important intermediate giving rise to more stable adaptive genotypes.
source_text: it appears that aneuploidies (Figure 7A, green), while largely transient, may be an important intermediate giving rise to more stable adaptive genotypes in some cases
